title: Navarin of Lamb
subtitle: French spring lamb stew with new-season vegetables
excerpt: The classic French spring braise: lamb shoulder pieces simmered in wine and stock with turnips, new potatoes, peas, and young carrots. Light for a stew, and a showcase for first-of-the-season vegetables.

recipe.sourceNotes: Navarin d'agneau printanier (spring lamb stew) is one of the most celebrated seasonal dishes of the French table, a braise that is explicitly designed to showcase the new-season vegetables of April and May alongside the young lamb that appears at the same time. The dish is lighter in colour and texture than a standard winter braise because it does not rely on heavy sauce thickening or strong aromatics; instead, the natural sweetness of the early vegetables provides the character. The name navarin is thought to derive from navet (turnip), the vegetable most associated with the dish. Classical recipes from Escoffier and Bocuse specify the printanier (spring) version, with young turnips, baby carrots, new potatoes, and fresh peas, as distinct from the winter navarin made with larger, harder vegetables.

recipeTools.notes: A wide casserole or large saucepan with a lid.

content.text: Brown the lamb in batches over high heat so it colours without steaming: colour equals flavour. A spring navarin should be lighter in the final result than a winter braise; use a young Bordeaux or lighter red wine rather than a heavy one. Add the most delicate vegetables (peas and the very smallest turnips) only in the final 10 minutes so they stay bright.

items.preparation: small, quartered; or 2 medium turnips, diced

content.text: Season the lamb with salt and dust lightly with flour. Brown in batches in a large casserole in hot oil over high heat until deeply coloured. Remove and set aside. Add the garlic and tomato purée to the pan and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits. Add the stock, thyme, and bay leaves.

Return the lamb to the pan. Cover and simmer very gently for 45 minutes. Add the new potatoes, carrots, and turnips and continue cooking, covered, for a further 25 minutes until the vegetables are just tender.
Add the peas in the final 5 minutes of cooking. Remove the thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Scatter with chopped parsley and serve directly from the casserole.
